items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push. 30-60 Day Post-Install Clients
items.preview:
**Audience:** Referral push candidates (30-60 days post-install, satisfied). **30 members**
Why this one first: these people just paid you, the install is fresh, the water change is tangible, and they haven't been blasted to death. Highest intent-to-advocate window you have. Small list = inbox-safe.
### Subject line (primary)
`The water's different now, right?`
**Alternates (varied hooks):**
- Curiosity: `One question since your install`
- Pain: `Who else is drinking that water?`
- Authority: `We only grow one way (and it's not ads)`
- Specific: `$500 when a neighbor says yes`
### Preview text
`If someone asked about your water this month, here's what that's worth.`
### Email body
> Hi [First Name],
>
> It's been about a month since we installed your ClearWave system, so you've had time to actually live with the difference. The glasses are clearer. The skin feels different. People notice.
>
> Here's the only ask we ever make: if a friend, neighbor, or family member mentions their water, send them our way.
>
> If they book a consult, you get a **$50 gift card**. If they become a client, you get **$500 cash** (and it climbs to $750, then $1,000 as you refer more through the year).
>
> They get a **free water assessment**. No pressure, no script, just a straight answer about what's in their water.
>
> Just reply with a name and the best way to reach them, and we'll take it from there.
>
>. Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(Note: Sherwin, Teronda, Lori, Daniel are inside the 30-60 day window with real/zero totals; copy uses the tenure line rather than any system name, since several are "(not specified)" and others carry legacy names like "FerroMax" / "H20 Protector." No legacy name printed.)*
### Send timing
**Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET**. Mid-morning weekday, strongest B2C open window, avoids Monday clear-out.
### Expected performance
- **Open: 48-55%.** Well above your 42.3% average because this is a tiny, recently-engaged segment with a personal, non-salesy subject. These people chose you weeks ago.
- **Click/reply: 6-10%.** Your broad campaigns click at 0.27%, but this is a reply-driven CTA (no link to click), and the audience is warm. A handful of named referrals is the realistic win.
- **Conversion: 2-4 booked consults.** At your bonus structure, even 1 closed referral justifies the send.
### Source justification
Draws from **REFERRAL BONUS STRUCTURE** (exact $500/$750/$1,000 tiers + $50 gift card), **HARD RULE 3** (referrals over reviews), **HARD RULE 3a** ("free water assessment" verbatim), and **HARD RULE 2** (tenure line, no legacy names). Audience from Jobber "Referral push candidates (30-60 days)."

items.title: Email Campaign · : Concierge "Is It Worth It?". Year 1.5 Clients
items.preview:
**Audience:** Concierge upsell candidates (13-24 months post-install, not on Concierge). **100 members**
Why second: these clients have already been through their year-1 annual service, so they trust the service experience. They're past the 12-month hard floor. This is your highest-dollar recurring-revenue play ($99/mo) and the list is big enough to matter but warm enough to open.
### Subject line (primary)
`The question everyone asks at year one`
**Alternates (varied hooks):**
- Curiosity: `Is Concierge actually worth it for you?`
- Pain: `Who's tracking your filter swaps? (nobody)`
- Authority: `Here's the honest math on $99/mo`
- Specific: `Annual service, filters, parts: one plan`
### Preview text
`No pressure. Just the math on whether Concierge makes sense for your home.`
### Email body
> Hi [First Name],
>
> It's been a little over a year since we installed your ClearWave system, which means you've had your first annual service and you know how we work.
>
> So here's the question we get asked most around this point: "Is the Concierge thing actually worth it for me?"
>
> Fair question. Here's the honest math.
>
> Concierge is **$99/mo**, and it covers:
> - Your annual service (already built in)
> - Filter swaps on schedule, so you're never guessing
> - Priority phone support when you need a human fast
> - Parts coverage on your standard install components
>
> If you'd rather stay pay-as-you-go, that's completely fine. This isn't a hard sell. It's for the folks who'd rather never think about their water again and have it all handled.
>
> Want me to run the numbers for your specific setup? Just reply "Concierge" and I'll send your breakdown.
>
>. Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(Note: list includes legacy names like "Reionator Pro + RO," "Pro Ultra + RO," "Orbit Customer". None printed. Tenure line used throughout. "Samantha Brutlag" completed 2025-10-24 is ~6 months out, under 12 months in that row; **she must be filtered OUT before send** despite appearing in the sample. Confirm every recipient is genuinely 13+ months post-install.)*
### Send timing
**Thursday, 11:00 AM ET**. Later in the week signals "considered decision," not impulse; late-morning catches the inbox check.
### Expected performance
- **Open: 40-46%.** Near your account average. Larger list drags it slightly, but the subject is curiosity-driven and the audience trusts the service after year 1.
- **Click/reply: 3-5%.** Reply-driven ("reply Concierge"). Even at the low end on 100 contacts, that's 3-5 real conversations.
- **Conversion: 2-5 Concierge sign-ups.** At $99/mo, 3 sign-ups = ~$3,500/yr recurring. This is your best revenue-per-send of the week.
### Source justification
Draws from **CONCIERGE UPSELL CONTEXT** (the "is it worth it at year 1.5?" framing, $99/mo feature list, non-pushy tone), **HARD RULE 1** (12-month floor. Enforced, with the Brutlag flag), and **HARD RULE 2** (tenure line, no legacy names printed). Audience from Jobber "Concierge upsell candidates (13-24 months)."
---
### Why only these two
I'm deliberately skipping the **1,000-contact cold re-engagement** and the **RO replacement** sends this week. The cold list is your biggest deliverability risk right now. Blasting 1,000 unengaged contacts while your opens are already depressed could trip spam filters and hurt the whole audience. That campaign deserves its own week, a warm-up plan, and a genuine news hook (per the cold-lead note). Let's prove the segmented approach lifts your numbers with these two small sends first, then earn the right to re-engage cold.
